title: Light-score v1
description: The compiled artifact the PC-side score compiler (Part 3) writes and the Pi-side firmware (Part 2) plays back. Device-independent: it carries musical facts only. LED indices are NOT stored here -- the firmware derives them from its own calibrated note map, so one light-score plays on any bar.

source.description: Which input arm produced this: a MIDI file, MusicXML, OMR over a PDF/photo, or audio transcription.

fingering.description: How the fingering was produced. 'dp' = generated by the fingering DP; 'score' = taken from fingering marks already in the source; 'manual' = hand-edited.

fingering_cost.description: Total DP path cost. Useful for regression-testing the cost model across releases; not used at playback.

tempo.description: Tempo map, for display and for re-deriving beats. Playback does NOT need it: every note already carries absolute milliseconds.

notes.description: Every note, sorted by onset t ascending. Short keys are deliberate: a dense piece is tens of thousands of notes and this is parsed on a 512 MB Pi Zero 2 W.

p.description: MIDI pitch. Bounded to the 88-key range A0..C8 -- anything outside cannot be shown on the bar.

h.description: Hand. Drives the left pixel of the 2-LED pair (D-12).

f.description: Finger, 1=thumb .. 5=little. Drives the right pixel's hue (D-12). This is the whole point of the format.

stf.description: Originating staff, 1=top. Display only; hand assignment lives in h.

v.description: Velocity, if the source had one.
